value="<b><br>Q: Why a separate back channel?</b> <br><br><p>Think of <strong>front channel = browser</strong> and <strong>back channel = direct server-to-server communication</strong>.<br><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><br>Why separate back channel?<br></span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Because </span><strong style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">tokens are sensitive</strong><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">.</span></p><p>Instead of:</p><p><code dir="ltr">Browser → Authorization Server → Token → Browser</code></p><p>we prefer:<br><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Browser → Login<br></span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Backend → Authorization Server → Token</span></p><p>So the <strong>token stays away from the browser</strong>, reducing the chance of it being stolen.</p>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="235" width="265" x="995" y="627" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-33" parent="1" div.b: Q: Why a separate back channel?
div.p:
Think of front channel = browser and back channel = direct server-to-server communication.
Why separate back channel?
Because tokens are sensitive.

we prefer:
Browser → Login
Backend → Authorization Server → Token
So the token stays away from the browser, reducing the chance of it being stolen.
